question_stem:
A sphere floats in equilibrium on the surface of sea water of density $1050\text{ kg m}^{-3}$, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
$21\%$ of the volume of the sphere is below the surface of the water.

Calculate the density of the sphere.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: The sphere is now held so that its entire volume is below the surface of the water. The sphere is then released.
parts.text: Calculate the initial acceleration of the sphere.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The sphere accelerates upwards but remains entirely below the surface of the water.

State and explain what happens to the acceleration of the sphere as its velocity begins to increase.
